protocol_overview.type: Host-mastered storage protocol layered on PCI Express. Host submits 64-byte commands into a Submission Queue ring in host memory and signals the controller via a single MMIO doorbell write (SQyTDBL); the controller fetches commands via PCIe Memory Read TLPs, executes them, posts 16-byte completions to a Completion Queue ring in host memory via PCIe Memory Write TLPs, signals the host via MSI-X / MSI / INTx, and the host releases CQ slots via the CQyHDBL doorbell.
protocol_overview.transport: PCI Express (NVMe over PCIe — Base 1.4 binding). NVMe over Fabrics (RDMA, TCP, Fibre Channel) is a separate specification that re-binds the same protocol shape onto fabric transports.
protocol_overview.duplex: Asymmetric: host writes SQ doorbells; controller writes CQ entries and CQ-side memory writes; no shared bidirectional wire — the underlying PCIe link is full-duplex.
protocol_overview.host_role: Bus master at the storage-protocol layer — fills SQ entries, rings the SQ Tail Doorbell, consumes CQ entries, rings the CQ Head Doorbell. Allocates SQ + CQ memory in host memory (or in Controller Memory Buffer if supported).
protocol_overview.controller_role: Slave at the storage-protocol layer — fetches SQ entries via PCIe MRd, executes commands, returns data via PCIe MRd/MWr, posts CQ entries, generates MSI-X interrupts.

functional_requirements.text: The controller shall expose its register set in PCI BAR0/BAR1 (MLBAR/MUBAR) mapped to memory space supporting in-order access and variable widths. The host shall access registers in native width or aligned 32-bit accesses; locked accesses are prohibited (Section 3 normative).
Offset 0h shall implement the 64-bit CAP register exposing MQES, CQR, AMS, TO, DSTRD, NSSRS, CSS, BPS, MPSMIN, MPSMAX, PMRS, CMBS (Section 3.1.1).
Offset 8h shall implement the 32-bit VS register; a 1.4-compliant controller shall report MJR=1, MNR=4, TER=0 (Section 3.1.2.6).
Offsets Ch and 10h shall implement INTMS / INTMC (used only with pin / single-message MSI / multi-message MSI). Host shall NOT access these registers when configured for MSI-X (Section 3.1.3/3.1.4).
Offset 14h shall implement the 32-bit CC register exposing IOCQES, IOSQES, SHN, AMS, MPS, CSS, EN (Section 3.1.5). CC.EN transitions 0→1 enable the controller; 1→0 triggers a Controller Reset.
Offset 1Ch shall implement the 32-bit CSTS register exposing PP, NSSRO, SHST, CFS, RDY (Section 3.1.6). RDY transitions 0→1 within CAP.TO × 500 ms after CC.EN=1.
Offsets 24h/28h/30h shall implement AQA (ASQS+ACQS, 12-bit each) and ASQ/ACQ (52-bit MSBs of 64-bit physical base addresses, memory-page aligned per CC.MPS).

Offset 1000h shall be the first SQ0 Tail Doorbell (SQ0TDBL); offset 1000h + (1 × (4<<CAP.DSTRD)) shall be CQ0HDBL. Subsequent SQyTDBL / CQyHDBL pairs shall follow at stride (4 << CAP.DSTRD) per Section 3.1.24/3.1.25.

Each SQ entry shall be 64 bytes laid out per Figure 105: bytes 0:3 = CDW0 (CID + PSDT + FUSE + OPC); 4:7 = NSID; 8:15 = reserved; 16:23 = MPTR; 24:39 = DPTR (PRP1+PRP2 or SGL1); 40:43..60:63 = CDW10..CDW15 (command-specific).
Each CQ entry shall be at least 16 bytes: DW0 = command-specific; DW1 = reserved; DW2 = SQID:SQHD; DW3 = SF:P:CID where P = Phase Tag, SF = 16-bit Status Field (DNR+M+CRD+SCT+SC).

On entering controller-enabled state (CC.EN 0→1), all CQ Phase Tag bits shall be initialized to 0; the controller inverts the Phase Tag bit each pass through the Completion Queue ring. Host uses the inverted Phase Tag in CQE.DW3 bit 16 to detect newly posted completions without consulting a doorbell.

PRP entries shall be 64-bit Page Base Address + Offset, where the Offset width follows CC.MPS (e.g. 12 bits for 4 KiB pages). PRP entries within a PRP List shall have zero offset; PRP2 may be a PRP List pointer if the transfer exceeds one memory page.

When CDW0.PSDT=01b or 10b, the command shall use SGL descriptors instead of PRP. SGL Data Block, Bit Bucket, Segment, Last Segment, Keyed Data Block, and Transport SGL Data Block descriptor types shall be supported per the controller's reported SGL Support.
Queue ID 0 shall be the Admin SQ/CQ pair, sized 2..4096 entries; the Admin Submission Queue shall accept only commands defined in the Admin Command Set (Section 5).

I/O queues created via Create I/O Submission Queue (0x01) and Create I/O Completion Queue (0x05) shall accept commands from the selected I/O Command Set (NVM Command Set is the only Set defined in v1.4).

A Submission Queue Tail Doorbell write moves the Tail entry pointer past the slot(s) the host just filled; the controller fetches SQ entries in order but may execute in any order. A Completion Queue Head Doorbell write moves the Head past the slot(s) the host just consumed; the slot is then available for the controller to reuse.
Three reset levels shall be supported: PCIe Conventional / Function-Level Reset; NVM Subsystem Reset (NSSR write of 0x4E564D65, optional per CAP.NSSRS); Controller Reset (CC.EN 1→0).
Pin / single-MSI / multi-MSI hosts shall use INTMS/INTMC to mask/unmask interrupt vectors; MSI-X hosts shall use the MSI-X table mask bits instead.

The Asynchronous Event Request command (Admin OPC 0x0C) shall remain outstanding; the controller completes one AER per asynchronous event with the event class (SMART, Notice, Error, Vendor Specific, ANA, Reserved) encoded in DW0 of the completion.
Every Completion Queue entry shall carry the current SQ Head Pointer in CQE.DW2[15:0]; this is the only mechanism for the controller to advance the host-visible SQ Head.
Two adjacent SQ entries with FUSE = 01b (first) and 10b (second) form a Fused Operation; the controller shall complete them atomically (Compare-and-Write being the canonical example).

configurations.name: Single PCI Function, single Controller
configurations.description: Most common single-NVMe-SSD shape (Figure 3); PCI Function 0 = NVMe Controller with one or more namespaces.

configurations.name: Multi-Function, multi-Controller, single port
configurations.description: Figure 4; both controllers map to PCI Function 0 / Function 1 sharing namespaces (Multi-Path I/O / Namespace Sharing).

configurations.name: Multi-port, multi-controller
configurations.description: Figure 5; each PCIe port has its own controller, with shared namespaces between them for HA / multipath.

configurations.name: SR-IOV
configurations.description: Figure 6; one Physical Function + N Virtual Functions, each presenting an NVMe Controller; SR-IOV configuration via the Virtualization Management Admin command.

configurations.name: NVMe over Fabrics
configurations.description: Same protocol shape rebound to RDMA / TCP / Fibre Channel transports (separate specification).

error_response_conditions: Invalid Command Opcode (0x01) — reserved or unsupported opcode in CDW0.OPC.
Invalid Field in Command (0x02) — reserved or unsupported value in a defined field.
Command ID Conflict (0x03) — CID already in use on the same SQ.
Data Transfer Error (0x04) — transient PCIe / fabric data error.
Internal Error (0x06) — fatal controller error, often paired with CSTS.CFS=1.
Command Abort Requested (0x07) — explicit Abort (0x08) command targeted this command.
Aborted due to SQ Deletion (0x08) — host deleted the SQ while commands were outstanding.
Invalid SGL Segment / Length / Type / Number — SGL malformed (0x0D..0x11).
PRP Offset Invalid (0x13) — non-zero offset where zero required, or non-page-aligned PRP.
Invalid Namespace or Format (0x0B) — NSID is invalid or format is incorrect.
Invalid Queue Identifier / Size / Deletion / Interrupt Vector — Create/Delete I/O Queue specific status (Section 4.6.1.2.2).
Invalid Doorbell Write Value — writing past Tail / Head; raises Asynchronous Event with Invalid Doorbell Write Value notice.
Controller Fatal Status (CSTS.CFS=1) — non-recoverable error; controller stops processing.
Path-related status (SCT=3h) — ANA-related or transport-related path status.
compliance_requirements: Host shall not issue commands to an I/O SQ unless CSTS.RDY=1 and CC.EN=1.
Host shall not modify AQA, ASQ, ACQ while CC.EN=1 (Section 3.1.8).
Host shall not issue Create I/O Submission Queue before its associated Create I/O Completion Queue.
Host shall delete all I/O Submission Queues associated with an I/O Completion Queue before deleting that Completion Queue (Section 4.1).
Host shall ensure CC.IOSQES / CC.IOCQES match the controller's required Submission/Completion Queue Entry Size for the selected I/O Command Set (Identify Controller SQES/CQES, Figure 247).
Host shall verify CAP.MPSMIN ≤ CC.MPS ≤ CAP.MPSMAX before enabling the controller.
Host shall handle the Phase Tag inversion across CQ ring wraps to correctly identify new completions.
Host shall not write to a non-existent doorbell — undefined results.
Host shall wait for CSTS.RDY=0 after CC.EN 1→0 before re-enabling the controller (CSTS.RDY transitions per Section 7.3).
Controller shall complete CC.EN 0→1 with CSTS.RDY=1 within CAP.TO × 500 ms.
Controller shall complete Normal Shutdown (CC.SHN=01b) by setting CSTS.SHST=10b before the host removes power.
Controller shall return 0h for all reserved registers and reserved bits within registers (Section 1.5).
